[THOUGHT] A 22-year-old with 2 days of fever and new altered mentation, high fever (39.6°C), tachycardia, normal glucose, no seizures, no focal deficits, and a normal noncontrast head CT. In adults the most common cause of sporadic encephalitis is herpes simplex virus (HSV); presentation often includes fever and altered mental status and may lack headache, neck stiffness, or focal signs early, and CT can be normal initially. Bacterial meningitis is less likely given absence of severe headache/meningeal signs; metabolic/toxic causes are less likely with normal glucose and no other systemic abnormalities identified. Therefore the single most likely diagnosis is HSV encephalitis.

[DIAGNOSIS] Herpes simplex virus (HSV) encephalitis

judge_response:
ANALYSIS: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome is an acute drug‑induced syndrome (typically from antipsychotics) characterized by severe rigidity, hyperthermia, autonomic instability, altered mental status, and markedly elevated CK. HSV encephalitis is an infectious encephalitis causing fever, focal neurologic deficits, seizures, and altered consciousness due to viral invasion of the brain. They are distinct etiologies and clinical syndromes and are not clinically equivalent.

VERDICT: INCORRECT
